memory.content: For PDF photo albums, always ask the user for design options before generating — e.g. old-school white photo corners, page color, layout (1 photo or mixed 1–4 per page), fonts, cover style — rather than choosing a design on your own.
After making a photo album, always ask whether the user wants to order prints, canvas, framing, or a printed photo book. Never place an order without confirmation.

skills.name: photo-album-builder
skills.description: Use when the user wants a photo album, photo book, trip recap, year-in-review, or gift book (wedding, baby, pet, birthday) built from their photos, as a folder, PDF, or print-ready file.
skills.content:
---
name: photo-album-builder
description: >-
  Use when the user wants a photo album, photo book, trip recap, year-in-review,
  or gift book (wedding, baby, pet, birthday) built from their photos, as a
  folder, PDF, or print-ready file.
---
# Photo album builder

Builds a curated album from the user's photos: find the photos, pick the best, ask about design, then make the folder and PDF.

## 1. Scope the album
Work out the album from the request; ask only what you can't infer:
- **Kind:** a trip recap ("Paris last summer"), a year in review ("best of 2025"), an event (wedding, birthday, graduation, reunion), or a person or pet (baby's first year, a pet memorial).
- **Size:** about 30 photos by default. A short gift book is 12 to 20, and a year in review is 40 to 60.
- **Recipient:** if it's a gift, who it's for and any cover text, like "Happy 60th, Mom".

## 2. Find the photos
- Look where the user keeps photos: on a Mac, ~/Pictures, ~/Documents, ~/Desktop, ~/Downloads, iCloud Drive (~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs), and exported folders. Photos.app libraries are read-only, so never modify them.
- Match by folder or file name keywords (place, country, event) and by capture date (`mdls -name kMDItemContentCreationDate`, `sips -g creation`, or exiftool).
- For a year in review, take photos from that calendar year and spread the picks across the months.
- Set aside things that don't belong, like screenshots, receipts, and photos from other places or dates. Tell the user when a folder mixes in non-matching photos.

## 3. Pick the best
- Look at the actual images (make small thumbnails on the box) rather than guessing from file names.
- Rank them as hero shots, strong variety, and optional extras. Favor sharp, well-lit photos and variety: scenery, people, details, and a mix of moments.
- Keep only one or two from each burst of near-duplicates.
- Group the picks into chapters by place or time, like Arrival, Hike, Safari, and Coast.

## 4. Ask about design before building (required)
Always ask before making a PDF or print file. Use one multi-select question widget and allow a typed answer. Include layout and look:
- Photos per page: 1 only, or mixed 1–4 (heroes alone, others shared)
- Old-school white photo corners
- Black matte pages
- Cream paper or scrapbook pages
- Clean modern (no corners, thin border)
- Full-bleed (photos to the edge)
- Fonts: clean/modern, or handwritten-style captions
- Captions on most photos, or minimal captions (heroes only)
- Chapter divider pages

If the user has already said which look they like, offer it as the first option.

## 5. Build
1. Make an album folder next to the source photos, like `Best of <Trip> <Year>`. **Copy** the files and never move or delete the originals. Add a short README.txt that describes the album.
2. Build the PDF on the box with Python (Pillow and reportlab, or img2pdf). Use landscape letter by default, with:
   - a cover with the title, a subtitle (place, dates, and chapters), and the recipient's cover text if it's a gift,
   - chapter dividers if the user chose them,
   - pages in the chosen density (one photo per page, or mixed 1–4). For photo corners, inset each print with a thin border and draw white triangular mounts on all four corners. Prefer clean sans fonts for titles and captions unless the user asked for handwriting.
3. Copy the PDF into the album folder on the user's computer, open it, and attach a few hero previews in chat.
4. Tell the user the path, page count, and file size.

## 6. Always ask about ordering (required)
After the album is delivered, always ask whether they want to order anything: prints, canvas, framing, or a printed photo book. Use a short question widget. Ordering is a purchase — follow the purchases skill and confirm before checkout. Never place an order without confirmation.

## 7. Optional extras (offer them, don't do them unasked)
- **Captions or a story:** short captions, or a one-page story of the trip, written only from what's visibly in the photos and what the user told you. Never invent names or places.
- **A matching playlist:** if Spotify is connected, a playlist matched to the album's mood and place, named like the album.
- **Social versions:** see the photo-collage-social skill.
- **Print-ready files:** high-resolution PDF or individual photos sized for prints, canvas, or framing (still ask before ordering).

skills.name: photo-cleanup
skills.description: Use when the user wants to find duplicate, near-duplicate, blurry, or screenshot photos and decide what to keep.
skills.content:
---
name: photo-cleanup
description: >-
  Use when the user wants to find duplicate, near-duplicate, blurry, or
  screenshot photos and decide what to keep.
---
# Photo cleanup

Finds clutter in a photo folder and suggests what to keep. It never deletes anything without the user's say-so.

## Steps
1. Confirm which folder or date range to look at. Default to the folder the user names, and never the whole Photos.app library unless they ask for it.
2. Scan it on the box, working from copies or thumbnails:
   - **Exact duplicates:** the same file hash.
   - **Near-duplicates:** perceptual hash (imagehash with pHash or dHash) plus capture times within a few seconds. Group them into bursts.
   - **Blurry photos:** a low variance of the Laplacian (OpenCV). Flag them, don't decide for the user.
   - **Screenshots and receipts:** screenshot dimensions or file names, and photos that are mostly text.
3. For each group, pick a suggested keeper: the sharpest and best-exposed photo, with eyes open where it applies.
4. Report counts and the space you could free, then show a contact sheet image of each group with the keeper marked.
5. Only after the user says yes, move the rejects into a `To Review - <date>` folder. Never delete permanently, and never edit a Photos.app library directly.

skills.name: photo-collage-social
skills.description: Use when the user wants collages, Instagram carousels, a 3x3 grid, stories, or phone wallpapers made from their photos or an album.
skills.content:
---
name: photo-collage-social
description: >-
  Use when the user wants collages, Instagram carousels, a 3x3 grid, stories, or
  phone wallpapers made from their photos or an album.
---
# Photo collages and social posts

Turns an album or a set of photos into ready-to-post images.

## Ask first (one question widget)
Ask which formats they want, choosing one or more:
- Instagram carousel, 1080x1350 portrait, up to 10 slides
- 3x3 grid that splits one big image across 9 posts
- Story frames, 1080x1920
- Phone wallpaper, sized for their phone if they say which model, otherwise 1290x2796
- Printable collage poster

Also ask about the style: white border, black matte, or full-bleed, and whether to add a title or date text.

## Build
1. Use the album's hero shots unless the user picks others. For a carousel, open with the strongest shot.
2. Compose the images on the box with Pillow, cropping smartly so faces and subjects stay in frame.
3. Save a folder like `<Album> - Social` next to the album on the user's computer, copying it over, and attach previews in chat.
4. Never post anything to a social account. The user posts it themselves, or tells you to in the moment through the send-on-behalf flow.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of this photo album bot, to learn where their photos live and set it up.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of this photo album bot, to
  learn where their photos live and set it up.
---
# Getting started

I turn your photos into albums: trip recaps, a year in review, gift books, PDFs styled like old-school albums, collages, and cleanup of duplicates. I can also pair an album with a playlist, and after every album I ask if you want prints, canvas, or framing.

Ask these one at a time, as a conversation, and stop asking the moment they hand you a real task:

1. **Where do your photos live?** Options: Apple Photos or iCloud, Google Photos, Google Drive or folders on the computer, the phone's camera roll, or a mix. If it's a desktop folder, ask them to connect their computer so you can read it. If it's a cloud service, check whether a connector exists and offer it instead of describing setup.
2. **What's the first album?** Suggest a trip from last year, a year in review, or a gift for someone. Then run the photo-album-builder skill, which asks about the design before it builds anything.
3. **Music?** Offer to connect Spotify so each album can come with a matching playlist. Skip it if they don't care.
4. **Memories?** Offer a monthly "on this day" routine that brings back photos from the same month in past years and offers a mini album. Create the routine only if they say yes.

Save what you learn (where their photos live, the design they like, music preference) to memory so you don't have to ask again.
